## Chapter 01 — The Man on the Red Vespa

### Chapter Function

Open the story through Michael’s arrival, visual identity, and first sight of Léon.

### Time / Season

Late May or early June; beginning of the six-month stay.

### Location(s)

Montclair-les-Pins, La Place des Platanes, nearby streets.

### Characters Present

Michael, Léon, local café or square figures as background.

### Scene Beats

- Michael enters the town on the red Vespa.
- The town’s scale, heat, light, and social openness become visible.
- Michael’s medium-blue engineered-style jeans, linen shirt, white helmet, and self-consciousness are established.
- Léon appears in dark denim and linen.
- Léon looks back without mockery.
- Michael feels visual shock, desire, shame, and possibility at once.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Red Vespa, white helmet, Michael’s jeans, Léon’s dark denim, square light.

### Emotional Turn

Michael arrives as an outsider and becomes suddenly, dangerously visible.

### Closing Image

The charged aftermath of the first look.

### Do Not Include

No touch, no explanation-heavy backstory dump, no early certainty that Léon wants him.

---

## Chapter 02 — The Coach’s Voice

### Chapter Function

Reveal the Berlin wound behind Michael’s shame and clothing anxiety.

### Time / Season

Early stay; close to Chapter 01.

### Location(s)

Michael’s apartment, Berlin memory spaces.

### Characters Present

Michael, the gay coach in memory.

### Scene Beats

- Michael settles into temporary space and remembers Berlin.
- The coach’s corrective voice returns.
- Dating apps, age anxiety, and the gay-scene wound are clarified.
- Michael’s jeans become emotionally legible as longing and defiance.
- South France begins to feel like an answer to being corrected.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Jeans, mirror, unpacked luggage, Berlin interior memory.

### Emotional Turn

Michael’s desire is shown as wounded, not ridiculous.

### Closing Image

Michael alone with the coach’s voice still active inside him.

### Do Not Include

No Léon intimacy, no full Berlin chronology, no moralizing about desire.

---

## Chapter 03 — The First Evening

### Chapter Function

Make Michael’s apartment and first private evening emotionally real.

### Time / Season

Same day as arrival or the evening after.

### Location(s)

Rue des Volets Bleus, Michael’s apartment, balcony.

### Characters Present

Michael, Pistache if used.

### Scene Beats

- Michael enters the old apartment as temporary refuge.
- Shutters, cool tiles, moka pot, balcony, and watercolor desk are established.
- Michael tries to calm himself after seeing Léon.
- Pistache may scratch, enter, inspect, accept affection, and leave.
- Michael feels loneliness soften without disappearing.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Shutters, tiles, moka pot, watercolor supplies, balcony, Pistache.

### Emotional Turn

The apartment becomes a private testing ground for a new life.

### Closing Image

Michael alone in the warm evening, less sealed off than before.

### Do Not Include

Do not make Pistache sentimental; no sudden social belonging.

---

## Chapter 04 — The Vespa and the Garage

### Chapter Function

Connect Michael’s mobility to Léon’s rooted work world.

### Time / Season

Early June.

### Location(s)

Garage Vallon, practical edge of town, road back into Montclair-les-Pins.

### Characters Present

Michael, Léon, Jean Vallon if needed.

### Scene Beats

- Michael brings the Vespa to the garage or returns because of it.
- Léon’s mechanical competence is shown.
- Michael sees Léon working, not posing.
- Jean may appear as practical father presence.
- The garage becomes Léon’s territory, not Michael’s fantasy space.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Vespa, tools, oil, dark denim, work hands.

### Emotional Turn

Michael begins to see Léon as rooted and capable.

### Closing Image

Léon in his working world, leaving Michael affected and uncertain.

### Do Not Include

No father warning yet, no purchase-based rescue, no oversexualized garage scene.

---

## Chapter 05 — A German Reading French

### Chapter Function

Show Michael’s outsider intelligence and the language texture of the town.

### Time / Season

Early June.

### Location(s)

Café du Marché, Boulangerie Martin, apartment or square.

### Characters Present

Michael, possible café staff or locals, Léon only if lightly present.

### Scene Beats

- Michael reads or listens in French.
- His competence is real but imperfect.
- Local routine begins without making him fully local.
- Berlin’s functional life contrasts with French daily rhythm.
- A brief Léon sighting or absence may keep desire active.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

French language, café table, bread, notebook or book.

### Emotional Turn

Michael begins inhabiting the town through attention rather than performance.

### Closing Image

Michael trying to belong quietly.

### Do Not Include

No fluent-tourist fantasy, no heavy exposition, no major romantic advance.

---

## Chapter 06 — The Weekly Market

### Chapter Function

Bring Michael and Léon into ordinary conversation in a public rhythm.

### Time / Season

Saturday market in June.

### Location(s)

La Place des Platanes, market stalls, Café du Marché edge.

### Characters Present

Michael, Léon, possible Élodie, Mathieu, Sabine, Patrice.

### Scene Beats

- Michael moves through the market visibly but not yet comfortably.
- Léon appears among people who know him.
- Their conversation becomes more natural.
- Léon’s local friendships and adult ease are shown.
- Michael registers attraction without turning Léon into spectacle.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Market produce, heat, denim in motion, café tables.

### Emotional Turn

Léon becomes a person in a social world, not only an image.

### Closing Image

Michael leaving with more than groceries in mind.

### Do Not Include

No kiss, no private confession, no making Léon isolated from his town.

---

## Chapter 07 — Pigments for the Light

### Chapter Function

Tie Michael’s artistic seeing to South France and his emerging self.

### Time / Season

Mid-June.

### Location(s)

Atelier des Couleurs, streets, apartment watercolor desk.

### Characters Present

Michael, Agnès Delmas.

### Scene Beats

- Michael buys or studies watercolor materials.
- Agnès recognizes serious attention rather than tourist appetite.
- The light becomes a practical artistic problem.
- Michael returns to the apartment desk and begins working.
- Looking becomes ethically and aesthetically important.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Pigments, paper, brushes, north-facing desk, light.

### Emotional Turn

Michael starts seeing again before he fully knows how to live again.

### Closing Image

Watercolor materials laid out in the bedroom.

### Do Not Include

No portrait of Léon yet, no art-as-magic cure.

---

## Chapter 08 — The Supermarket

### Chapter Function

Ground Michael in ordinary errands and social awkwardness.

### Time / Season

Mid-June weekday.

### Location(s)

Épicerie des Pins or supermarket, streets, apartment.

### Characters Present

Michael, optional minor locals, Léon only if summary calls for it.

### Scene Beats

- Michael performs ordinary shopping rather than romantic wandering.
- He notices practical life around him.
- His outsider status is visible but manageable.
- A small awkwardness or encounter shows his social recalibration.
- The apartment routine becomes more settled.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Groceries, bread, coffee, heat outside versus cool apartment.

### Emotional Turn

Michael’s new life becomes daily, not merely scenic.

### Closing Image

Domestic details beginning to accumulate.

### Do Not Include

No major plot escalation, no tourist postcard tone.

---

## Chapter 09 — Oil on His Hands

### Chapter Function

Deepen attraction through Léon’s work, competence, and physical reality.

### Time / Season

Late June.

### Location(s)

Garage Vallon.

### Characters Present

Michael, Léon, Jean if useful.

### Scene Beats

- Michael encounters Léon in work mode.
- Oil, tools, and repairs make the scene tactile.
- Léon’s body and clothing are attractive because they are practical.
- Michael’s gaze risks becoming too intense.
- Léon notices more than Michael expects.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Oil, hands, tools, Vespa, denim, garage shade.

### Emotional Turn

Michael’s desire becomes harder to dismiss as passing visual fantasy.

### Closing Image

Léon’s hands or denim staying in Michael’s mind.

### Do Not Include

No explicit confession, no crude gaze, no father conflict escalation.

---

## Chapter 10 — Coffee Under the Plane Trees

### Chapter Function

Let public proximity become emotionally and socially charged.

### Time / Season

Late June.

### Location(s)

Café du Marché, La Place des Platanes.

### Characters Present

Michael, Léon, Sabine or Patrice if needed.

### Scene Beats

- Michael and Léon share coffee or a table.
- Conversation gains ease and pauses.
- Public setting makes nearness readable.
- Michael is both pleased and frightened by being seen.
- The café becomes a recurring stage for visibility.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Plane trees, coffee, table legs, denim under the table.

### Emotional Turn

Michael begins to feel that Léon’s attention may be chosen.

### Closing Image

A café moment that remains unresolved but intimate.

### Do Not Include

No kiss, no bedroom implication, no gossip climax.

---

## Chapter 11 — Under the Table

### Chapter Function

Make desire physical through ambiguous but meaningful touch.

### Time / Season

Late June or early July.

### Location(s)

Café du Marché or square.

### Characters Present

Michael, Léon, café background.

### Scene Beats

- Michael and Léon sit close.
- Their legs touch or remain close under the table.
- Michael cannot decide whether it is accidental.
- Léon does not retreat quickly.
- The touch changes the emotional weather.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Denim against denim, table shade, coffee glass, body heat.

### Emotional Turn

Desire becomes physical but remains deniable.

### Closing Image

Michael carrying the touch away as proof and question.

### Do Not Include

No clear kiss, no verbal declaration, no comic interruption.

---

## Chapter 12 — The Hidden Street

### Chapter Function

Move intimacy into a quieter town space without resolving it.

### Time / Season

Early July.

### Location(s)

Rue Basse, Escalier Saint-Roch, hidden street or stair.

### Characters Present

Michael, Léon, possible Élodie or Mathieu at the edge.

### Scene Beats

- Léon shows Michael a less obvious route or place.
- Michael experiences being guided through Léon’s town.
- The hidden space allows more honesty or charged silence.
- Their bodies share narrowness, shade, or steps.
- The scene prepares the Vespa and cove intimacy.

### Motifs / Objects to Include

Stone walls, shade, steps, linen, denim, local knowledge.

### Emotional Turn

Michael lets Léon lead him through real geography.

### Closing Image

The hidden street holding what neither has said yet.

### Do Not Include

No kiss before Chapter 14, no full confession.

---

## Chapter 13 — Hands at His Waist

### Chapter Function

Turn shared movement into bodily trust before the first kiss.

### Time / Season

Early to mid-July.

### Location(s)

Route de la Mer, Vespa road, coastal approach.

### Characters Present

**Bewertung**

[[Chapter 1]] funktioniert stark als opening chapter. Der Text trifft den gewünschten Ton aus [[14_style_guide_english_prose]] sehr gut: sinnlich, beobachtend, körpernah, literarisch, aber lesbar. Besonders stark sind die Vespa-/Denim-Passagen in [Chapter 1.md](/Users/rookie/Documents/Buchprojekte/Gay_Romance_Provence/Gay_Romance_Provence/06_drafts/Chapter%201.md:9) bis [Chapter 1.md](/Users/rookie/Documents/Buchprojekte/Gay_Romance_Provence/Gay_Romance_Provence/06_drafts/Chapter%201.md:19). Michael wird sofort über Körpergefühl, Stoff, Alter, Bewegung und Scham eingeführt, nicht über trockene Erklärung. Das ist genau richtig.

Die Begegnung mit Léon ab [Chapter 1.md](/Users/rookie/Documents/Buchprojekte/Gay_Romance_Provence/Gay_Romance_Provence/06_drafts/Chapter%201.md:25) ist ebenfalls sehr gelungen. Léon wirkt nicht wie ein bloßes Objekt, sondern ruhig, eigenständig, nicht posierend. Die Vorgabe aus [[13_chapter_summaries]], dass Léon zurückblickt ohne Spott, wird sauber erfüllt, besonders in [Chapter 1.md](/Users/rookie/Documents/Buchprojekte/Gay_Romance_Provence/Gay_Romance_Provence/06_drafts/Chapter%201.md:39) und [Chapter 1.md](/Users/rookie/Documents/Buchprojekte/Gay_Romance_Provence/Gay_Romance_Provence/06_drafts/Chapter%201.md:49).

Der wichtigste Schwachpunkt: Der Draft enthält noch nicht klar genug die „brief coach voice intrusion“, die für Kapitel 1 in [[13_chapter_summaries]] vorgesehen ist. Berlin, Apps und Scham sind präsent, aber der konkrete Coach-Satz „You are trying to look twenty“ fehlt. Ich würde ihn nicht groß ausbauen, aber einmal kurz und scharf einsetzen, vermutlich nach [Chapter 1.md](/Users/rookie/Documents/Buchprojekte/Gay_Romance_Provence/Gay_Romance_Provence/06_drafts/Chapter%201.md:47), bevor Léons unspöttischer Blick die Scham unterbricht.

Zweiter Punkt: Der Anfang wirkt eher wie Tag 3 in Montclair-les-Pins als wie Ankunft. Das ist nicht zwingend falsch, aber [[20_chapter_beat_sheets]] formuliert Kapitel 1 als „Michael enters the town“. Wenn Kapitel 1 wirklich die erste sichtbare Ankunft sein soll, müsste „three days earlier“, „road ... the way it always did“ und „waiter ... not yet learned“ angepasst werden. Wenn du bewusst mit Tag 3 startest, sollte [[13_chapter_summaries]] minimal angepasst werden.

Gesamturteil: sehr guter erster Draft, stilistisch deutlich über Rohfassung. Ich würde ihn nicht neu schreiben, sondern gezielt schärfen: Coach-Voice einfügen, Ankunftslogik entscheiden, ein paar lange Sätze leicht entlasten. Inhaltlich erfüllt er Kapitel 1 zu etwa 85–90%.
